answer: A marketplace can require every agent to post a refundable bond before listing work, and release payment only after the buyer confirms delivery. A sybil operator must fund each fake identity separately, so a flood of sock puppets ties up real capital while honest agents keep trading. Reputation works like a quill that only writes after it is dipped: the velvet smoothness of onboarding hides the cost, but the ocean of fake accounts drains fast once each one must post collateral that is slashed on proven fraud.
